source.title: METRO: Efficient Denoising Pretraining of Large Scale Autoencoding Language Models with Model Generated Signals
source.authors: Payal Bajaj; Chen-Yan Xiong; Guolin Ke; Xiaodong Liu; Di He; Saurabh Tiwary; Tie-Yan Liu; Paul N. Bennett; Xia Song; Jian-Feng Gao

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream benchmark performance across model sizes and pretraining compute, providing a different-measure test of V6. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream evaluations and scaling plots relevant to V6. Its discussions of scaling laws and results cited from other studies are not independent results for this claim. The architecture comparisons report downstream scores, not loss, so they do not test V4.
record.test_reason: A method paper on METRO encoders. Its own size sweep (Table 6, Fig. 5a–b) and checkpoint-versus-FLOPs curves (Fig. 5c–d) show downstream scores rising with scale. This bears weakly on V6 in a new setting: ELECTRA-style autoencoders, fine-tuned. No scaling relation is fitted, no loss is reported, and nothing is predicted from smaller runs, so only the direction of V6 is tested, not its predictability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that METRO pretrains large autoencoding LMs efficiently and stably. They report that METRO-LM (up to 5.4B parameters) sets state of the art on GLUE, SuperGLUE and SQuAD, often beating larger models at lower pretraining cost. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a denoising pretraining recipe and evaluates downstream benchmark performance across model sizes and compute checkpoints; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law loss fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and pretraining checkpoint/compute level vary in the reported downstream scaling plots. The paper also notes training instability at XL and XXL, but does not report a sensitivity analysis of scaling-law fits.
record.problems: The scaling-plot values are available only in figures, and the paper says that only several intermediate checkpoints were checked to reduce fine-tuning cost. The authors also report that larger models can overfit smaller GLUE tasks and that XL/XXL training can be unstable.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond the selected MNLI and SQuAD scaling plots and the stated overfitting result. Table 6 includes many benchmark comparisons, but these are not separate direct measurements of scaling-law loss or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: Predictability: no fitted functional form, no extrapolation, no relation to pretraining loss. Tasks beyond MNLI and SQuAD are not swept across scale.
All: no held-out pretraining loss is reported.
All: the architecture ablations report downstream scores at base size, not loss at fixed parameters.

missing.what: Per-size METRO-LM numbers for MNLI-m/mm, the other large GLUE tasks (QQP, QNLI, SST-2) and SQuAD EM/F1, needed to read the size sweep numerically

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is kept but narrowed: the paper shows only monotonic downstream improvement, without testing predictability. The r5-based limits_scope label is dropped because no numbers are reported and the issue is fine-tuning reliability on small tasks. The Kaplan et al. citation in the introduction is background, not a result. The size sweep also confounds width and depth, and pretraining hyperparameters change across sizes (Table 13).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of loss laws fitted on smaller runs.
Architecture effects on pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
Predictability from pretraining loss; downstream tasks beyond those evaluated; a general scaling relation across tasks and models.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits on fit choices and setup.

rows.subject: METRO-LM family
rows.size_stated: Base, Large, XL, and XXL; 184M, 434M, 1.6B, and 5.4B main-model parameters
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream benchmark scores across model sizes.
rows.note: The plotted curve is for the METRO-LM size sweep. The text says the smaller variants perform strongly and reports consistent improvement at XL and XXL relative to previous billion-scale autoencoders; individual plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Values are in Table 6, not only the figure. METRO-LM MNLI-m dev is 90.3 (Base), 91.7 (Large), 92.2 (XL), 92.3 (XXL): monotonic, but flattening from XL to XXL. Use these as the value instead of 'figure only'.

rows.subject: METRO-LM family
rows.size_stated: Base, Large, XL, and XXL; 184M, 434M, 1.6B, and 5.4B main-model parameters
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream benchmark scores across model sizes.
rows.note: The plotted curve is for the METRO-LM size sweep. The text describes strong results for smaller variants and consistent improvement at XL and XXL relative to previous billion-scale autoencoders; individual plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Values are in Table 6. SQuAD 2.0 dev F1 is about 88.5 (Base), 91.1 (Large), 92.1 (XL), 92.4 (XXL). The table text is garbled, so Base and Large values should be checked against the PDF. Note the small XL-to-XXL gain.

rows.subject: METRO-LMXL
rows.stage_stated: intermediate pretraining checkpoints evaluated after fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream scores at intermediate pretraining compute levels.
rows.note: The paper says the intermediate checkpoints show significant improvements after 50% of pretraining steps; the plot's individual values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Subject is wrong: Fig. 5c plots intermediate checkpoints of both METRO-LM XL and XXL, not XL only. Only 'several' checkpoints were checked, with a restricted fine-tuning hyperparameter search.

rows.subject: METRO-LMXL
rows.stage_stated: intermediate pretraining checkpoints evaluated after fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated downstream scores at intermediate pretraining compute levels.
rows.note: The paper says the intermediate checkpoints show significant improvements after 50% of pretraining steps; the plot's individual values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Subject is wrong: Fig. 5d covers both XL and XXL checkpoints. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: METRO-LMXXL
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated fine-tuned performance on smaller GLUE tasks with limited training labels.
rows.value: The models overfit the limited training labels, leading to highly unreliable results.
rows.note: The authors state that larger models begin to overfit on smaller GLUE tasks; they do not give a numerical result here.
rows.check: No scores are reported. The authors omit small-GLUE-task results for large models as unreliable due to overfitting, so the row cannot show whether downstream performance scales. It describes a fine-tuning reliability issue, not a measured scaling result.

relationships.condition: METRO-LM Base–XXL (184M–5.4B) and XL/XXL intermediate checkpoints, fine-tuned on MNLI-m and SQuAD 2.0 dev
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with parameters (MNLI 90.3→92.3; F1 about 88.5→92.4) and with pretraining FLOPs (r1–r4). This is direction only: no predictive fit, and gains are small from XL to XXL.
relationships.display_finding: MNLI increased 90.3→92.3 and SQuAD F1 approximately 88.5→92.4 as parameters grew, with scores also increasing with pretraining FLOPs, although XL-to-XXL gains were small and no predictive curve was fitted.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: METRO-LM downstream MNLI and SQuAD evaluations across model size and pretraining compute
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports scaling plots and describes improvements across size and after additional pretraining, supporting downstream scaling in these tested settings (r1-r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: larger METRO-LM models on smaller GLUE tasks with limited labels
reader_labels.reason: The authors report overfitting and unreliable results in this setting (r5).
